Grenoble → Geneva by train, 17–24 October 2026

Slow-paced, rail-only, historic towns and lake scenery, a walk most days.

Getting there and back (booked)

  • Sat 17 Oct: train from Tilburg via Brussels and Lyon, arriving Grenoble 18:39.
  • Sat 24 Oct: flight from Geneva at 17:15 (KLM to Amsterdam). Be at Genève-Aéroport by 16:15.

Where you sleep

Seven nights, four places. Book an apartment, B&B or hostel in each.

Route spine

All on the TER Auvergne–Rhône-Alpes line Grenoble–Chambéry–Aix-les-Bains–Annecy, then Léman Express L2 into Geneva. Under 4 hours of train in the whole week.

Leg Time Notes
Grenoble → Chambéry ~55 min TER; sparser on Sundays
Chambéry → Aix-les-Bains ~12 min very frequent
Aix-les-Bains → Annecy ~30–35 min TER
Annecy → Genève-Eaux-Vives ~1h15 Léman Express; every 2 h on Saturday mornings

One short train hop between each base.

Day by day

Sat 17 Oct — Arrive Grenoble · night in Grenoble

Train arrives 18:39. Book near the station.

Sun 18 Oct — The Bastille, then Chambéry · night 1 of 2, Chambéry

Morning: up to the Bastille fort above the city, for the view over Grenoble and the Alps. Cable car from 09:15 on Sundays (€6.60 one way), or walk up through the Jardin des Dauphins, about 260 m of ascent. Midday train to Chambéry (Sundays: 11:31 or 11:58, ~45–50 min). Afternoon in the old town: the covered allées and traboules, the Fontaine des Éléphants, and the Cathédrale Saint-François-de-Sales, whose vaulting is trompe-l'œil rather than carved.

Mon 19 Oct — Mont Saint-Michel, above Challes-les-Eaux · night 2 of 2, Chambéry

Bus line C to Challes-les-Eaux (~15 min), starting from the thermal park. About 400 m of ascent, 3–4 h round trip, to a chapel on a rocky knoll with views over the Combe de Savoie and the Bauges. Chambéry's museums close on Mondays, so this is the day for it.

Tue 20 Oct — Les Charmettes, then Aix-les-Bains · night 1 of 2, Aix-les-Bains

Morning: Les Charmettes, the house where Rousseau lived with Mme de Warens 1736–42 (Tue–Sun, 10:00–18:00; ~35 min walk uphill from the centre). Early-afternoon train to Aix-les-Bains. Afternoon: the Temple of Diana, the Arch of Campanus, the Thermes Nationaux, the Belle Époque quarter, the Grand Port.

Wed 21 Oct — Abbaye de Hautecombe by boat · night 2 of 2, Aix-les-Bains

Boat from the Grand Port across the Lac du Bourget: about 2 h 30 return with 1 h 30 ashore, ~€18.50. Twelfth-century Cistercian abbey, and the necropolis of the House of Savoy. Wednesday because the abbey closes Mondays and Tuesdays from 20 September. Confirm sailings by phone — see Verify.

Thu 22 Oct — Aix-les-Bains → Annecy · night 1 of 2, Annecy

Optional morning walk: the flat Voie Verte along the Lac du Bourget shore, 7 km to Le Bourget-du-Lac (~2 h), or turn back at Tresserve. Both ends have a station. Midday train to Annecy. Afternoon: the canals, the Palais de l'Isle, the Musée-Château, the Pâquier.

Fri 23 Oct — Lake Annecy · night 2 of 2, Annecy

SIBRA bus 20 to Echarvines/Talloires (~45 min), then the Roc de Chère nature reserve loop: a wide forest path, 1.5–2 h, to a belvedere over the lake and the Château de Duingt. The Château de Menthon is nearby (April–October; confirm the October days). Alternative: the flat Voie Verte from Annecy to Duingt (12 km), bus back.

Sat 24 Oct — Annecy → Geneva, flight home · no night

10:44 train from Annecy, Genève-Eaux-Vives 11:58 (Saturday mornings run every two hours; the 08:44 gives a longer day). Léman Express on to Cornavin, 15 min, and leave bags in the station lockers. A few hours in the old town: Cathédrale Saint-Pierre, the lakefront. Back at Cornavin by 15:30; the airport is 7 min by train. Flight 17:15.

Ruled out (checked)

  • Gorges du Fier — season ends 15 October. Closed for this trip.
  • Le Revard and the Semnoz — the mountain buses (S11 from Aix; Rando'Bus 40/41 from Chambéry) run in summer and winter only. No car-free access in October.
  • Hautecombe on Mon or Tue — abbey closed those days from 20 September.
  • Les Charmettes on Monday — closed.

Verify before booking

  • Hautecombe cruise, October sailings. Shoulder-season departures are not published online. Compagnie des Bateaux du lac d'Aix-les-Bains, 04 79 63 45 00.
  • Château des ducs de Savoie. The Sainte-Chapelle is guided-tour only and the October schedule is reduced. Chambéry Montagnes tourist office, 04 79 33 42 47.
  • Engineering works. Grenoble–Chambéry electrification is ongoing, and some Sunday services run as replacement coaches from the bus station; an Annecy–Annemasse closure runs 14 Sep–9 Oct 2026 (ends before the trip). Recheck ter.sncf.com/auvergne-rhone-alpes closer to the date.
  • Château de Menthon — October opening days.

Practical

  • School holidays. France (Toussaint): 17 October–2 November, all zones. Geneva: 19–23 October. The whole trip falls in them. Book beds early, Annecy first, and note SNCF often schedules track work in that window.
  • Tickets. TER fares are cheap and need no advance booking. The Léman Express crosses the border — buy a through ticket to Geneva, or a Swiss ticket from Annemasse.
  • Weather. Roughly 5–15 °C in the pre-Alps, morning fog on the lakes, first snow above ~1,800 m. Layers, waterproofs, boots for Mont Saint-Michel.
  • Daylight. Sunset around 18:45. Clocks go back on 25 October, the day after you fly home.
